title: Title
description: FlowForge brand title slide with tagline and product positioning
speakerNotes:
Open by acknowledging the room knows this pain personally.

- Every buyer here has a WhatsApp group with a factory they've never met in person.
- They have a shared sheet someone is always behind on updating.
- FlowForge is the single workspace that replaces the fragmented stack — not by asking suppliers to change, but by connecting to what they already use.
- Deck takes 20 minutes. Happy to go deeper on anything.

title: The Problem
description: Three pain points: 47+ message threads, 4+ disconnected channels, days lost to late detection
speakerNotes:
Let the numbers do the work — don't explain them, just let the audience sit with them.

- 47 threads per shipment is a conservative estimate for teams managing 50+ POs.
- Four channels means four different apps open simultaneously, no unified history.
- The 'Days' stat is the one that costs money: by the time a delay is visible, it's too late to reroute or expedite.
- Ask: 'How many of you found out about a delay from a WhatsApp message that someone on your team missed?' — pause for hands.

title: Why Now
description: Three market forces creating urgency: AI-first procurement, board-level supply chain mandate, process fragility at 50+ POs
speakerNotes:
This slide creates urgency without pressure tactics — let the market forces speak.

- AI: buyers who adopt AI-assisted procurement tools now are compounding an advantage. The cost of waiting is falling further behind peers who are already using extraction and drafting.
- Visibility: post-disruption, every executive team has a slide in their board deck about supply chain resilience. FlowForge directly addresses that requirement.
- Scale: this is the internal urgency driver. Teams growing from 20 POs to 80 POs hit a wall where their current process breaks. That wall is usually painful enough to drive a decision.
- Ask: 'Which of these three resonates most with where your team is right now?' — the answer tells you which value prop to lead with.

title: Origin Story
description: We built this for ourselves first — the founding team's pain, the cost of delayed discovery, and the decision to build the communication layer
speakerNotes:
This is the trust slide. Tell the story, don't pitch it.

- The founding team ran sourcing operations across factories in Asia and LATAM. This isn't a tool built by engineers who heard about supply chain — it's built by people who lived the problem.
- Do NOT name a specific company. Say 'our founding team' — that's the right level of generality at this stage.
- The cost example (expedited freight, markdown) is relatable to anyone in the room who has had a similar experience. Let them connect it to their own story.
- The quote at the bottom is the positioning anchor: the problem is structural (no unified place), not operational (bad suppliers or tools).

title: What FlowForge Does
description: Condensed product overview: communication + coordination layer, four capabilities, what it is not, AI's supporting role
speakerNotes:
This is the 'so what' slide. Keep AI in its supporting role — it's not the headline.

- The key framing: FlowForge is not a new channel. It sits on top of the channels they already use.
- Four capabilities, not five — we've tightened the messaging. The inbox, AI assist, stage tracker, and risk+payments are the four pillars.
- The 'what it is NOT' panel is one of the most important parts of this slide. Pre-empt the ERP and monitoring objections before they're raised.
- 'Zero supplier onboarding' is the clearest competitive advantage. Reinforce it here before going into detail.
- Transition: 'Let me show you exactly how it fits into a real workflow.'

title: How It Fits the Workflow
description: Forwarding and companion-app model: how messages arrive, honest about no passive monitoring, SAP/Oracle integration as scoped project
speakerNotes:
This is the honesty slide. Prospects respect it.

- Walk through each ingestion method: forward from WhatsApp chat exports, email via Postmark, mobile app for on-the-go pasting.
- Explicitly address passive monitoring before they ask: 'We don't silently read your WhatsApp groups. Ingestion is buyer-initiated. This is a deliberate choice for compliance and trust.'
- SAP/Oracle: say it upfront. 'ERP integration is possible and supported, but it's priced and scoped separately. We won't promise it's included and then surprise you.'
- The honest pitch at the bottom is the close for this slide: 'Start with 5 shipments in 2 weeks. Prove it before you commit.'

title: Ideal Customer Profile
description: Primary: retail and apparel buyers with 20-200 active POs. Secondary: sourcing agencies. Not the primary fit: trade finance intermediaries.
speakerNotes:
Use this slide to confirm where the prospect fits — then tailor the rest of the conversation.

- Primary ICP is the retail or apparel buying team managing 20–200 active POs across 2+ channels. The economic buyer is VP Supply Chain or Head of Sourcing.
- Secondary ICP is the sourcing agency — multiple clients, multiple suppliers, needs audit trail and compliance. COO or Director of Operations.
- Trade finance: we support the three-party payment model, but position it as a module, not the core. Don't lead with it in pilot conversations.
- The qualifying question on the right side is the single most useful thing on this slide. Ask it: 'How many active POs, and how many channels?' — 20+ POs across 2+ channels is a FlowForge prospect.

title: ROI
description: Directional early metrics: 50% faster response times, 30% fewer shipment surprises, 80% reduction in manual tracking
speakerNotes:
Frame these as directional indicators, not audited proof — that framing makes them more credible, not less.

- 50% faster responses: the mechanism is clear — AI draft + full context means no digging. A buyer who used to spend 15 minutes per reply now spends 3.
- 30% fewer surprises: risk scoring surfaces delays before they become crises. The window to act is what has value — rerouting a shipment costs less than a markdown.
- 80% reduction in manual tracking: this is the one that resonates with ops-focused buyers. The math is simple: reply once, tracker advances automatically, team sees it.
- After presenting: 'The pilot is designed to help you measure your own version of these numbers. We'll baseline you in week 1.'
- The disclaimer is important and earns trust: say it aloud — 'These are directional, not audited. The pilot will show you your specific numbers.'

title: Before / After
description: Two-column comparison: before (scattered, reactive, manual) vs after (centralized, structured, automated) across 5 operational dimensions
speakerNotes:
Let the audience read this one. It's designed to be scannable — resist the urge to narrate every row.

- Give them 30 seconds to read the slide. Then ask: 'Which row resonates most with your team right now?'
- The delay detection row is usually the most painful — finding out 3–5 days late is the one that costs the most money.
- The document handling row lands with finance and compliance teams — re-keying PDFs is everyone's least favorite task.
- If they're nodding at multiple rows: 'The good news is FlowForge addresses all of these simultaneously — they're all connected to the same structural problem.'

title: Competitive Landscape
description: Wedge framing: ERPs, Anvyl (closest overlap), Flexport/freight tools, and custom builds. FlowForge as the only option with zero supplier behavior change.
speakerNotes:
Lead with the framing, not the table: 'We're not claiming no one else exists. The real question is what job each tool is hired for.'

- ERPs: 'They record what happened. We surface what's happening. Different jobs.'
- Anvyl is the closest overlap — acknowledge it directly. 'The key difference: Anvyl requires your suppliers to log into their portal. We don't ask suppliers to change a single thing.'
- Freight tools: 'Complementary. They handle the freight leg; we handle the communication leg. Some of our customers use both.'
- Custom builds: 'This is the real default competitor — everyone's got their Airtable base and their Slack thread. The question is whether it scales to 50+ POs. Usually it doesn't.'
- Close: 'Our wedge is the only option that requires zero supplier behavior change while giving the buying team structured, AI-assisted coordination.'

title: Pilot Structure
description: 3 months free: two-week setup, live on a contained workflow, monthly feedback calls, measure and decide at month 3
speakerNotes:
The pilot removes risk from the decision. Present it as disciplined, not desperate.

- 'Three months free' is the headline. 'No commitment, no contract' is the close.
- The key framing: 'We designed the pilot to be contained and measurable. 5–10 shipments, a defined scope, monthly calls. It's structured so you can run it alongside your existing process — no disruption to how you operate today.'
- Monthly feedback calls are mutual: 'We want to hear what's working and what's missing. Your input directly shapes what we build next.'
- Month 3 is the decision point: 'You'll have three months of data. Expand, adjust, or walk away — we've designed it so you can make a fully informed decision.'

title: What Pilot Proof Will Look Like
description: Placeholder for proof: what gets measured, anonymized case study format, buyer controls what gets published
speakerNotes:
Honesty here builds more trust than a fabricated testimonial.

- 'We don't have testimonials yet. We're being deliberate about who we pilot with. What we can show you is exactly how we'll measure and document the results.'
- Walk through the four metrics — response time, delay detection lag, manual tracking hours, thread fragmentation. These are the ones that show up in every lost-deal debrief.
- The anonymized format: 'Company type, team size, baseline, monthly snapshots, one-paragraph qualitative. Shared only with your approval.'
- The quote at the bottom is the close: 'One real before/after from a team like yours is worth more than ten testimonials from teams you can't relate to.' Let that sit.
- If they push for references: 'I'd rather let you be the first to measure this for your context than refer you to someone in a different business model.'

title: Pricing
description: Founding member pricing: $99/month or $1,000/year. Enterprise and custom integrations scoped separately.
speakerNotes:
Lead with the founding member framing — it's the correct context for the number.

- '$99/month or $1,000/year — that's the founding member rate. Teams that pilot with us and convert lock this in. It won't be the rate we charge when we have case studies and a full sales motion.'
- Annual is the better conversation: '2 months free, founding pricing locked, priority access to new features. Most teams find that's the right place to start.'
- Enterprise: 'If you're thinking about SSO, ERP integration, or custom channel configurations — those are scoped separately. I'd rather give you a number that's right than one that changes after discovery.'
- Custom integrations note: say it aloud — 'Custom integrations like SAP or Oracle are priced as separate scoped projects. The base subscription doesn't include them, and I want to be clear about that upfront.'
- If they push for a lower price: 'The pilot is free. The question is what happens at month 4, and that depends on what you've measured.'

title: Roadmap
description: Three roadmap chapters: supplier directory, localization (Chinese and Korean), and industry expansion beyond apparel
speakerNotes:
Keep this brief — the roadmap shows upside without muddying the current story.

- Supplier directory: 'This is the natural next step. Once buyers trust FlowForge for communication, they'll want to use it for discovery too. We'll build the directory around the suppliers already in the system.'
- Localization: 'Most of our target suppliers communicate in Mandarin or Korean. Removing the translation layer from the drafting step is one of the highest-impact things we can do. This is coming.'
- Industry expansion: 'Apparel and retail is the wedge. The same communication fragmentation exists in electronics, furniture, and food. We'll move category by category, not all at once.'
- If they ask about timeline: 'I'd rather not commit to dates and then miss them. These are the next three chapters — in that order.'

title: Pilot With Us
description: Three clear next steps: 3-month free pilot (5-10 shipments, 2-week setup), live walkthrough, or discovery call
speakerNotes:
End by giving them a clear choice — not a vague 'let us know.'

- The pilot is the strongest first step for anyone in the room who has a live PO problem right now. 'Five shipments, two weeks to live, no engineering. If it works, you'll know by month three.'
- The live walkthrough is for prospects who are still evaluating. 'Bring your hardest PO scenario — we'll run it through FlowForge live in 30 minutes. That's usually enough to know.'
- The discovery call is for enterprise scenarios. 'Custom org structure, ERP integration, complex requirements? Let's scope it before you commit to anything.'
- After presenting: ask directly — 'Which of these three makes the most sense as a first step for you?' — and stop talking. Let them answer.
- Email is pilot@flowforge.com — signals intent and makes the ask concrete.

title: Appendix — Platform Workflow
description: Line-art flow diagram showing the end-to-end FlowForgeIQ workflow: Channels → Ingest → AI Engine → FlowForge Hub → Outcomes
speakerNotes:
Use this slide when prospects ask 'how does it actually work under the hood?'

- Walk left to right: messages arrive from any channel (email, WhatsApp, WeChat, iMessage, SMS, documents). The buyer forwards or pastes them into FlowForge via email forward, chat export, mobile companion, or file upload.
- The AI engine extracts entities (PO number, dates, quantities), routes the message to the correct shipment thread, drafts a reply, and flags any risk signals (delays, discrepancies).
- Everything lands in the FlowForge Hub — the unified Inbox, Orders Grid, RFQ Manager, and Task Tracker — staged against the shipment lifecycle from Quote through Delivery.
- The outcomes on the right are what gets recorded automatically: stage progression, payment records, spread tracking, tasks, and a full audit trail.
- Key message: 'The buyer initiates every step. We never passively monitor anything. That's deliberate — compliance, trust, and simplicity.'

title: Team Walkthrough Cover
description: Cover slide for the RFQ-to-Shipment team walkthrough: scenario details (Chrome Retail Hangers, Tianjin Wire Works, Northbound Outfitters) and 9-part roadmap
speakerNotes:
Use this walkthrough section for new team member onboarding or as a live demo guide for pilot prospects.

- The scenario is realistic: Chrome Retail Hangers sourced from Tianjin Wire Works for Northbound Outfitters.
- Nine parts cover the full buyer workflow end-to-end — from creating an RFQ to uploading a document on mobile.
- Estimated time: 30–45 minutes for a first run-through; 15–20 minutes for team members who have done it before.
- Encourage participants to follow along in a live FlowForge session if possible.

title: Part 1 — Getting Oriented
description: Inbox overview: sidebar navigation, channel filter pills, message thread panel, AI draft reply, unread indicators and AI tags
speakerNotes:
Start here to orient new team members.

- The Inbox is the default landing page at flowforgeiq.com — there is no separate home page after sign-in.
- Walk through the sidebar: Inbox (home), Orders, RFQs, Copilot, Risk Radar, Settings.
- Channel filter pills allow fast scoping — useful when a team member is responsible for a specific channel (e.g. email only).
- The AI tags (risk, milestone, payment) are auto-generated — not manually assigned. Point them out early so team members know to look for them.
- Transition: 'Now let's create your first RFQ for the walkthrough scenario.'

title: Part 2 — Create the RFQ
description: RFQ creation: New RFQ modal walkthrough with field values for Chrome Retail Hangers, Northbound Outfitters buyer, target price $0.95, quantity 5,000
speakerNotes:
Creating an RFQ is the starting gun for the procurement workflow.

- The buyer name combobox supports both selecting from existing buyers and typing new ones — Northbound Outfitters should already exist in the seed data.
- Target price is critical: it's what FlowForge uses to compute 'cheapest' badges and savings percentage in the comparison table.
- Draft autosaves to session storage — participants can refresh the page if they make a mistake.
- After creation: the RFQ status is 'Open' and the Quotes tab is empty. The next step fills it.

title: Part 3 — Add Three Quotes
description: Quotes tab: adding three factory quotes (Tianjin Wire Works $0.87, Guangzhou Metalworks $0.91, Ningbo Alloy Co. $0.96) with lead times and MOQs
speakerNotes:
This is where the multi-supplier comparison begins.

- Add each quote using the '+ Add Quote' modal. Three quotes is the minimum for a meaningful comparison — participants should add all three.
- The quote status defaults to 'received' — there's also 'pending' for quotes still outstanding.
- Lead time and MOQ are important inputs: they feed the comparison table's fastest/cheapest badges.
- Ningbo Alloy at $0.96 is above the $0.95 target — the comparison table will flag this. That's intentional for the demo.

title: Part 4 — Compare Quotes & Pick a Winner
description: Quotes comparison table with cheapest/fastest badges, spread vs. target price, and Convert to PO button on the Tianjin Wire Works row
speakerNotes:
The comparison table is the most visually powerful part of the RFQ workflow.

- Ask participants: 'Which factory wins on price? Which wins on lead time? What would you pick?' — let them reason through it before revealing the badges.
- Tianjin Wire Works wins on both price ($0.87 vs $0.95 target) and lead time (28 days) in this scenario.
- The 'above target' badge on Ningbo Alloy is a deliberate signal — team members should learn to look for it.
- After picking a winner: click 'Convert to PO' to move to the next step. This is a one-way action — emphasize it.

title: Part 5 — Convert to PO
description: Convert-to-PO dialog: accepting quote, entering PO number, supplier, due date, ex-factory date, destination, via, and deposit percentage
speakerNotes:
Converting is the pivot point from sourcing to operations.

- All required fields must be filled before 'Convert' becomes enabled — enforce this with participants who try to skip.
- PO number format: use something memorable for the walkthrough, like PO-2026-HANGERS-001.
- Ex-factory date is typically 1–2 weeks before due date to allow for transit time.
- After converting: the RFQ status flips to 'Awarded' and a new row appears in the Orders grid. The two payment milestones (Deposit 30% / Balance 70%) are auto-created.
- Participants can optionally download a Proforma Invoice PDF immediately after conversion.

title: Part 6 — Track the Shipment
description: Orders grid: locating the new PO, shipment detail panel, stage tracker progression, spread badge, and stage advance workflow
speakerNotes:
The Orders grid is where day-to-day shipment management happens.

- New PO starts at 'Spec Sheet' — the first stage in the 11-stage lifecycle.
- Advance the stage to show how it works: click the arrow, confirm the transition, watch the stage history update.
- The spread badge is automatic: it recalculates every time payments are updated or the buyer price is set.
- Risk score appears in the right panel — mention that it factors in overdue payments, delayed stages, and unread messages.
- Encourage participants to explore the 'Docs' and 'Threads' tabs in the detail panel — they'll use these in real workflows.

title: Part 7 — Log a Payment
description: Payment milestone panel: marking the 30% deposit as paid with amount, date, payment method, invoice number, and reference fields
speakerNotes:
Payment logging is a critical operational step — it's what keeps the spread/margin calculation accurate.

- The Invoice Number field is required. Enforce this in real usage — it's the audit trail anchor.
- Method options: Wire, PayPal, Letter of Credit, Cash. Wire is the most common for factory payments.
- After marking paid: the milestone turns green, the balance due updates, and the spread recalculates.
- Participants often ask 'can we undo this?' — yes, there's an 'undo' action available immediately after marking paid.
- For the walkthrough: mark the 30% deposit as paid. Leave the balance for a later step or skip it to keep the session moving.

title: Part 8 — Mobile: Paste Supplier Chat
description: Mobile Capture tab: channel picker, WhatsApp export paste, sender hint, shipment linker, submit for routing, and routing result screen with confidence states
speakerNotes:
This is the moment where the mobile companion clicks for participants.

- Have participants use their own phones if possible — the demo is more visceral on a real device.
- The WhatsApp export flow: open WhatsApp → long-press conversation → More → Export Chat → share to FlowForge.
- If no real export is available: paste a realistic chat string into the text field. Use the example placeholder text in the app.
- Routing result: high confidence (green) means auto-routed. Medium (amber) asks to confirm. Low (red) sends to the web review queue.
- After confirming: the message appears in the web Inbox within seconds. Open the web app to show this in real time.

title: Part 9 — Mobile: Upload a Document
description: Mobile document upload: file picker, Documents tab, extraction review with confidence score, inline field corrections, and save corrections workflow
speakerNotes:
Document upload is the final step — it completes the walkthrough scenario.

- Use a real PDF if available: a quote sheet, packing list, or proforma from any supplier works.
- The extraction shows confidence percentage — 94% means the AI parsed most fields correctly.
- Inline corrections: tap any field, edit, save. This trains the extraction model over time.
- After saving corrections: the document is linked to the PO and appears in the web Orders → Docs tab.
- Close the walkthrough: 'You've now run the complete Chrome Retail Hangers scenario from RFQ to delivered document. Every step you just did is what your team will do on live POs.'
